hints: Compare the normal and mutated DNA base by base after GAT. Can you spot that one base (a T) is missing, so all the triplet groupings after that point are shifted?
Transcribe the mutated DNA triplets into mRNA codons and check them against UAG, UAA and UGA. Do you see any stop codon, and would a ribosome still be able to read a shifted message?
walkthrough:
**Spot the type of mutation**

Look closely after the first two triplets, CCG GAT, which are unchanged. The normal sequence continues TAT TGC GAG AAA TGG, while the mutated continues GTA TTG CGA GAA ATG.

If you write them as single bases, normal is TATTGCGAGAAATGG and mutated is GTATTGCGAGAAATG. One T has been deleted, so every triplet downstream is regrouped. This is a frameshift deletion.

**Check for mRNA stop codons**

A stop codon in mRNA is UAG, UAA or UGA. Transcribe the mutated triplets to mRNA, whether you treat the DNA as template or coding strand, none of them give UAG, UAA or UGA.

For example, as coding strand, GTA becomes GUA, TTG becomes UUG, CGA becomes CGA, and so on. So statement 1 is false.

**Decide on amino acids, protein function and translation**

Because the reading frame is shifted, different codons will be read, so different amino acids will be inserted. Statement 2 is true.

A changed amino acid sequence can alter folding and the active site, so a non-functional protein is a possible result. Statement 3 is true. Ribosomes can still attach and translate the altered mRNA, they just make an altered polypeptide, so statement 4 is false. That leaves 2 and 3 only.

options.A: Includes 1, which is wrong because no UAG, UAA or UGA is produced from the mutated sequence.
options.B: Includes 1 and 4, both wrong. There is no new stop codon and ribosomes can still translate the mRNA.
options.C: Claims 1 and 4 only, but both are false. Translation is not blocked and no stop codon appears.
options.D: Correct. The frameshift changes the amino acid sequence (2) which may give a non-functional protein (3), with no stop codon and no block to translation.
